investigations.name: copy-number-frontier
investigations.description:
The follow-up axis the first two maps did not sweep. Copy number is run at the exact corner
where speedup lives (system_size=100), so the live question — can a >=5x cell be made faithful
by raising abundance? — is directly testable. Because event_density re-solves the stochastic
rate scale against the propensity at X=N0, raising N0 leaves the per-unit-time event rate (and
thus the number of RK4 steps and stochastic events) fixed: copy number varies only the
intrinsic-noise level (CV ~ 1/sqrt(N0)) independently of every other axis. The mean/variance
z-score split (worst_abs_z_mean, worst_abs_z_var in the sweep JSON) separates the two stories:
the deterministic trajectory is accurate everywhere; what the partition drops is the continuous
species' intrinsic noise, and no copy number buys that back under a variance-sensitive gate.
investigations.title: Copy-number frontier: does high copy open a faithful-and-fast window?
investigations.objective:
The regime-frontier map found the only >=5x cells at large system size + low stochastic
fraction, all fidelity FAIL, and flagged copy number (held ~10-30) as the untested axis most
likely to open a faithful-and-fast window: high-copy continuous species should be well
approximated deterministically. Sweeping copy-number center N0 from 20 to 1000 at that
speedup corner (system_size=100, density=100), does raising copy number make any >=5x cell
faithful to exact SSA?
investigations.claim:
No. The map is FLAT in copy number. At N0 from 20 to 1000, every >=5x cell (stochastic
fraction <= 0.5; 10-11x at fraction 0.1, ~7x at 0.25) FAILS fidelity with worst |z| ~16, and
the value barely moves across a 50x copy-number range. The failure is entirely VARIANCE: the
deterministic mean is faithful at every copy number (worst |z_mean| ~2.5-5, at/below the |z|<=4
gate), but the hybrid gives continuous species ~zero intrinsic variance while exact SSA has
variance ~N0, so worst |z_var| stays ~16 regardless of copy number. The gap is copy-number-
invariant by construction, so copy number was never going to close it. Faithful cells remain
only at stochastic_fraction = 1.0 (fully stochastic, ~1x). 0 of 16 cells are both >=5x and
faithful. This resolves the open decision from regime-frontier and strengthens the
investigation verdict: no faithful-and-fast regime exists even with copy number swept.

investigations.name: regime-frontier
investigations.description:
The headline map. Speedup grows with system size and shrinks as stochastic fraction rises;
the fidelity mask (hybrid vs exact SSA, all species) passes only at fraction 1.0.
investigations.title: Regime frontier: system size x stochastic fraction
investigations.objective:
Sweeping system size against stochastic fraction (density 100), is there any cell that is
both >=5x faster than numba AND faithful to exact SSA?
investigations.claim:
No. The only >=5x cells are large systems at low stochastic fraction (10.8x at size 100 /
fraction 0.1; 6.8x at fraction 0.25), and both FAIL fidelity (worst |z| ~14-17). The
faithful cells (stochastic_fraction = 1.0) are ~1.0x. Fast and trustworthy are disjoint.

investigations.name: rust-engine-in-workbench
investigations.description:
Vertical slice. Composite viva_hybrid.composites.regime.rust_hybrid_benchmark drives the genuine run_ir binary and emits the engine's
simulate wall-time, RK4-step / stochastic-event counts, and mean protein level.
investigations.title: Rust engine runs the hybrid model in the workbench
investigations.objective:
Does the real compiled Rust hybrid engine run a hybrid ODE/SSA model end-to-end as a
process-bigraph composite inside the vivarium-workbench, and how does its per-run speed
compare to plain Python?
investigations.claim:
The Rust engine runs the bursting gene-expression benchmark as a workbench composite
(RustHybridStep bridging the real run_ir binary) and is ~30-50x faster than plain
interpreted Python per run.

investigations.name: speedup-landscape
investigations.description:
5x4 sweep via the regime harness. Speedup is modest and insensitive to event density; the
accuracy frontier tracks stochastic fraction, not density.
investigations.title: Speedup landscape: event density x stochastic fraction
investigations.objective:
Across event density and stochastic fraction (system size fixed at 10), how large is
the Rust-vs-numba speedup, and where is the hybrid faithful to exact SSA?
investigations.claim:
Rust/numba stays 1.3-2.6x and is nearly flat in event density; the hybrid is faithful to
exact SSA only at stochastic_fraction = 1.0 (where it is the exact path).
